subject: Sable Therapeutics — On-Prem Deployment Safeguards & Capability Questionnaire
messages:
From: Dr. Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@sablethera.com>
To: evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@sablethera.com>, procurement@sablethera.com

Subject: On-prem safeguards questionnaire follow-ups

Evelyn — thanks again for the quick turnaround on the questionnaire. We reviewed the initial responses and have three follow-ups that are blockers for our procurement and security teams before we move to a pilot: 

1) Binary/package signing: You indicated support for signed installers. Can you confirm what signing mechanisms you support (PKCS#7, GPG)? Is there an attestation process we can include in our SecOps runbook?

2) Patch windows for air-gapped sites: Our Ops teams require a defined update cadence and rollback plan for offline clusters. Can you provide the standard maintenance cadence, offline patch delivery methods, and an automated rollback procedure?

3) Telemetry/phone-home: For compliance, we must prevent any automatic outbound traffic without explicit, auditable approval. Please confirm which agent telemetry types are collected by default and how to disable outbound telemetry.

Can you also attach your operator runbook draft so our SREs can do a quick read? Carlos and procurement are looped in for scheduling a short technical call next week.

Thanks,
Aisha
Dr. Aisha Patel
Head of Infrastructure Security, Sable Therapeutics

From: evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Dr. Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@sablethera.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@sablethera.com>
Date: 2027-04-04T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem safeguards questionnaire follow-ups

Aisha — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, followed by an attached annex and the operator runbook draft (attached). See also the network diagram V2 we prepared for your team.

1) Signing: We deliver installers signed with PKCS#7 using our corporate code-signing CA. For air-gapped installs we can provide both a signed package and a detached signature file you can verify with your internal CA. We also support a GPG-signed artifact on request; see section 2 of the attached annex for the verification steps and sample commands.

2) Patching: Standard cadence for on-prem customers is quarterly security updates plus out-of-band critical patches. For air-gapped sites we provide: 
- signed delta bundles for incremental updates
- an offline package delivery (USB or secure transfer via your approved courier)
- an automated rollback hook in the operator that preserves the previous container image and KV cache snapshot for a 72-hour rollback window.
Detailed upgrade and rollback steps are in the runbook: Upgrade -> Preflight -> Apply -> Verify -> Rollback. We include preflight checks for kernel versions, free disk, and NVMe health.

3) Telemetry: By default our operator collects local metrics and logs to a customer-controlled path only. Outbound telemetry (cluster health to Redwood) is disabled in air-gapped mode. If enabled (for Hosted Remote Ops) it requires an explicit config flag, an operator-level opt-in, and an HMAC signed token. The runbook's telemetry appendix has the exact config boolean and sample systemd unit to manage the telemetry agent.

Next steps: Ben (cc) will join a technical sync to walk through the runbook and the signing verification. Marissa will coordinate procurement items and the mutual action plan. Proposed times: Tue 2027-04-06 10:00-11:00 PT or Wed 2027-04-07 15:00-16:00 PT. Let us know which works.

Attachments: sable_questionnaire_filled.xlsx; operator_runbook_draft.pdf; network_diagram_v2.pdf

—
Evelyn Hart
Enterprise Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-04-05T09:21:00-07:00
Subject: RE: On-prem safeguards questionnaire follow-ups — technical annex

Hi Aisha — following up with some low-level details that Ops will want: 

- Signing formats: our standard PKCS#7 signature is SHA256 with timestamping. For detached verification we include a .sig file and a small verification script: ./verify.sh --bundle bundle.tar.gz --sig bundle.sig --ca /path/to/ca.pem. If you prefer GPG we can provide a key and signatures instead.

- Delivery validation: each offline bundle includes a SHA256 manifest and an incremental delta id. The operator verifies the manifest before unpack, and the preflight fails if file hashes don't match.

- Rollback behavior: rollback preserves the previous model KV cache and container image. Operator performs the following steps on rollback: 1) stop new tasks, 2) restore image tag X, 3) restore KV cache snapshot, 4) warm KV cache from local snapshot, 5) resume traffic. We instrument the process with a safe mode flag that prevents automated fail-forward if health checks fail.

- Patch window: recommended maintenance window is 02:00-04:00 local, but can be customized. We advise a dry run in staging that mirrors your prod hardware.

I'll bring a short demo of the verification script to the call. Also included a stubbed sample manifest in the attached annex for your team to exercise.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference

- Can you supply a short test bundle and verification key ahead of the call so we can exercise the verification script in an isolated lab?
- In the rollback steps, how do you handle partial failures (e.g., image restores succeed but KV restore fails)? Is there an operator-level circuit breaker?

If you can drop the test artifacts to the Drive link you provided, we'll pull them into our lab tomorrow. Otherwise Tue at 10:00 PT works for us.

—Aisha
